01 · System overview

What the final stack contains

The production stack is a complete visual system with five visual modes, six sizes, 12 core post templates, an eight-slide carousel set, editable SVG masters, palette boards, design tokens, previews and Illustrator guidance.

5 visual systems

One identity with controlled alternative expressions.

6 sizes

Social, story, landscape and print-ready formats.

20 templates per size

12 core posts + 8 carousel slides.

600 SVG masters

5 × 6 × 20 editable vector templates.

02 · Governing principle

One recognizable HSF identity

The five palette systems are not five separate brands. They are professional visual modes under one Human Safety Foundation identity.

Identity remains stable. Expression adapts to purpose.

This principle prevents HSF from becoming visually inconsistent while still allowing project, campaign and communication needs to feel appropriate to context.

03 · Identity architecture

Stable identity, controlled expression

Institutional master

Evergreen

The default organization-wide system for HSF identity, general communication, community development, climate and evergreen projects.

Controlled alternatives

Blue · Gold · Red · Violet

Used deliberately for communication purpose, campaign meaning or project context.

Non-negotiable

Identity + dignity

Logo integrity, safeguarding, data verification and dignity standards do not change with palette.

04 · Five visual systems

Professional palette architecture

Evergreen remains the default. Alternative systems should be chosen because of communication purpose—not because a designer simply wants a different colour.

Visual system 1

Evergreen

Humanity, continuity & sustainable care

Best fit: HSF master identity, community development, climate, general project communication

Visual system 2

Trust Blue

Trust, peace & institutional credibility

Best fit: Human rights, WASH, health systems, global aid, partnerships, governance

Visual system 3

Hope Gold

Hope, energy & opportunity

Best fit: Youth projects, education, community mobilisation, celebrations, participation

Visual system 4

Care Red

Urgency, protection & compassionate action

Best fit: Emergency relief, health crises, protection, urgent advocacy, active response

Visual system 5

Dignity Violet

Dignity, inclusion & empowerment

Best fit: Women empowerment, safeguarding, inclusion, research, innovation, social protection

06 · Logo governance

The official logo does not follow campaign colour

The final stack intentionally does not trace or recreate the HSF logo. Every editable template contains an OFFICIAL_LOGO_PLACEHOLDER group so the approved vector master can be inserted.

  • Use the approved HSF vector logo in AI, SVG, EPS or vector PDF form.
  • Preserve proportions and clear space.
  • Do not recolour the HSF logo simply because a campaign uses Blue, Gold, Red or Violet.
  • A blue/red/gold/violet HSF logo should only be created if management formally approves a rebrand.
  • The campaign palette may change; the organization’s identity must remain recognizable.
Operational rule

Place the official logo into the placeholder layer. Do not treat alternative campaign palettes as permission to redesign the organization mark.

07 · Typography

Formal brand typography and operational social typography

Formal identity

Handel Gothic

Recommended formal HSF display typeface when licensed and available.

Official tagline

Monotype Corsiva

Reserved for the official tagline Always we are... where licensed and available.

Social English

Poppins

Primary working typeface for social media; Inter/Arial may be used as fallback.

Bangla

Noto Sans Bengali

Recommended Bangla working typeface.

The stack distributes no font files.

09 · Visual signature

Every HSF social design should answer five questions

1
Who? HSF
2
Which project / topic?
3
What is the message?
4
What evidence supports it?
5
What should the audience do?

This prevents attractive graphics from becoming disconnected from organizational identity, project context, evidence or meaningful audience action.

10 · Photo, evidence & accessibility

Humanity must remain credible, dignified and readable

Photo-led content priority

  1. Authentic HSF photography
  2. Real field environments
  3. Purpose-built infographic or illustration
  4. Stock only when clearly non-documentary
Do not present AI-generated beneficiaries as real HSF beneficiaries.

Public data rule

Value + metric + project + reporting period + source

Accessibility

  • Use mobile-readable type.
  • Maintain strong contrast.
  • Add captions to video and alt text where available.
  • Do not communicate meaning through colour alone.
  • Keep important text away from interface overlays.
  • Keep paragraph-length text out of images where possible.
11 · Production sizes

Six standardized aspect ratios

1:1
1080 × 1080

Square feed / paid carousel / broad compatibility

4:5
1080 × 1350

Primary Facebook / Instagram / LinkedIn feed

3:4
1080 × 1440

Portrait editorial / selected social layouts

4:3
1200 × 900

Landscape feed / presentations / web

9:16
1080 × 1920

Stories / Reel covers / vertical campaign cards

A4
2480 × 3508

Printable handout / report cover / poster

Default operating choices:
  • Feed: 1080 × 1350 (4:5)
  • Carousel: 1080 × 1350 (4:5) or 1080 × 1080 (1:1)
  • Story/Reel: 1080 × 1920 (9:16)
  • Landscape: 1200 × 900 (4:3)
  • Print/report: A4 portrait
  • Safe margin: approximately 4–6% of canvas
12 · Core post templates

Twelve reusable content families

Every core template family exists in all five visual systems and all six production sizes.

01

Project Story

Photo-led project communication with a human-centred headline.

02

Impact Number

One verified number with project, reporting period and source.

03

Impact Dashboard

Four verified results presented together as an impact snapshot.

04

Human Story

Approved field photo plus a short quote or hopeful headline; consent must be checked.

05

Awareness / Carousel Cover

A simple public-awareness hook designed to begin a swipe sequence.

06

Quote / Institutional Message

A short credible message connected directly to HSF work and values.

07

Event / Project Announcement

Event title, date/time/location and one clear action or contact.

08

Partnership / Recognition

HSF + partner identity with factual relationship context.

09

Volunteer / Recruitment

Role, eligibility/location and application method.

10

Support / Donation CTA

One specific verified outcome and what responsible support enables.

11

Report / Publication

Report, case study or policy brief promotion with read/download action.

12

Urgent Update / Crisis

Clear factual update, what happened and what people should do.

14 · Carousel system

Cover + complete inner-page storytelling architecture

Each visual system and size includes eight coordinated carousel pages. A carousel can use five to eight slides, but every slide should keep the same size, orientation and palette.

01
Slide 01

Cover / Hook

Why should I swipe?

A clear hook that makes people swipe. Keep the cover simple: one idea, one promise.

02
Slide 02

Context / Problem

What is happening?

State the context without sensationalism; use a short context point, a verified observation and a community implication.

03
Slide 03

Why It Matters

Why should people care?

Connect the issue to real-life outcomes and explain the human consequence.

04
Slide 04

HSF Response

What is HSF doing?

Explain the HSF response in three simple steps.

05
Slide 05

Evidence / Impact

What do verified data show?

Use only verified figures and include reporting period plus source.

06
Slide 06

Human Story / Photo

What does this mean for a person or community?

Use an approved HSF photo, a short human quote or insight and consent-checked context.

07
Slide 07

Action / Practical Steps

What can the audience do?

Give practical actions such as learn, discuss, share responsibly, volunteer, participate, partner or support.

08
Slide 08

Closing / CTA / Source

What is the next step and where is the evidence?

Close with one message, one clear next step and source or official contact when required.

Carousel rules:
  • Keep Slide 1 visually simple.
  • One slide = one idea.
  • Use page numbers such as 03 / 08.
  • Do not repeat the full logo at oversized scale.
  • Use the last slide for one CTA.
  • Keep long explanations in the caption rather than on cards.

16 · Illustrator workflow

How to turn SVG masters into working AI files

  1. Open the SVG in Adobe Illustrator.
  2. Open Window → Layers.
  3. Find the named groups such as logo placeholder, project badge, photo placeholder, editable content and footer.
  4. Replace the logo placeholder with the approved HSF vector logo.
  5. Replace placeholder text and photos.
  6. Keep the selected palette consistent.
  7. Save as a new .ai file and retain an editable master.
  8. Export final artwork separately as PNG/JPG or other required publication format.

Multi-artboard masters

For one theme, Illustrator can use 12 artboards for the core-post set or 8 artboards for a carousel set. All artboards in one carousel must use the same dimensions.

Carousel file export

01_Cover.png 02_Context.png 03_Why-It-Matters.png 04_HSF-Response.png 05_Evidence.png 06_Human-Story.png 07_Action.png 08_CTA.png

18 · Folder architecture

One master production folder

The final ZIP is structured so guidelines, palette references, production templates, previews, design tokens and Illustrator instructions remain separated but connected.

The template library then repeats the six format folders inside each of the five visual-system folders.

19 · Campaign consistency

Do not mix visual systems casually

Within one carousel, campaign or visual series:

  • Use one palette system.
  • Use consistent typography.
  • Use the same logo treatment.
  • Use the same page indicator and badge family.
  • Do not combine Gold cover + Blue inner pages + Red CTA unless the campaign has a deliberately approved colour-coded structure.
Use alternative palettes deliberately

Choose one because the communication purpose fits trust, hope, urgency or dignity/inclusion.

Avoid random variation

A different colour for every post weakens recognition and makes HSF look like multiple unrelated brands.

20 · Quality & export checklist

Before a design leaves the editable master

Brand & structure

  • Correct palette system
  • Official logo inserted
  • Logo proportions preserved
  • Project/topic badge correct
  • Consistent typography
  • Correct platform dimensions

Evidence & dignity

  • Facts verified
  • Reporting period included for data
  • Source included when relevant
  • Consent checked
  • No sensitive patient/student data
  • Human dignity preserved

Accessibility

  • Mobile readability checked
  • Strong contrast
  • Meaning not dependent on colour alone
  • Overlay-safe text placement
  • Alt text/captions prepared where applicable

Export

  • Keep SVG/AI as editable master
  • Export final PNG/JPG separately
  • Number carousel files in sequence
  • Archive final creative
  • Do not overwrite the master template
21 · Operating recommendations

A simple way to use a large 600-template system

The stack is large because it supports multiple systems and formats; daily production does not require browsing all 600 files. Use a narrow decision sequence:

Step 1
Choose purpose
Step 2
Choose one visual system
Step 3
Choose format
Step 4
Choose template family
Step 5
Insert verified content & export
Default shortcut:

When there is no special campaign reason, start with Evergreen → 4:5 → appropriate core template. For educational explanation, choose Evergreen or purpose-specific palette → 4:5 carousel → 5–8 slides.
